purpose: Prevent natural-language input from becoming executable shell, Python, SQL, or other arbitrary commands.

rules.rule: Natural-language text is never passed to a shell, Python interpreter, SQL engine, eval/exec, subprocess, workflow command, or notebook cell.
An intent resolver may propose only an exact task_id present in task-registry.v1.json; the proposal is not authorization.
Unknown, ambiguous, unsupported, or multi-intent requests are rejected or returned for clarification; no best-effort command construction.
Arguments must be structured values validated against the exact selected registry arguments_schema with additionalProperties=false.
Caller-supplied command strings, shell fragments, Python source, SQL, executable URLs, interpreter flags, and arbitrary workflow names are not accepted as task arguments.
Before handler lookup, validate authenticated actor, exact allow-listed repository, immutable commit SHA, envelope schema, expiry, and authorization policy.
No dynamic import, eval, exec, shell=True, command concatenation, or direct execution of user text in any handler.
Only fixed, reviewed handler_ref values in the versioned task registry may be resolved; no user-controlled handler names.
Destructive, external-side-effect, deployment, merge, credential, and live-data operations require a separate explicit approval gate and are not implied by natural-language intent.
If policy, registry, schema, identity, or repository verification is unavailable or fails, fail closed without executing a task.

execution_boundary.accepted_input: Untrusted natural-language text, used only to derive a candidate intent.
execution_boundary.permitted_output: A candidate fixed task_id plus JSON arguments; candidate must pass registry and authorization validation.
execution_boundary.prohibited_output: Shell/Python/SQL source, executable command strings, dynamic handler references, arbitrary workflow dispatch.
execution_boundary.runtime_status: Policy contract only; runtime enforcement and CI execution are not yet implemented or claimed.
